cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Not the Real Fear
cards.instruction: Keep the conversation focused on practical details so no one reaches the fear underneath them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll handle the move. Check my train time once more, then we'll talk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Six twelve. I've checked five times, and your ticket's in your hand.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All right, no more times. Check whether this ticket opens the barrier.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll walk you through the barrier. Are you scared of leaving me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can come that far. First, find out if you need a platform ticket; I'll hold the bags.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 claims management of the move; A3 concedes the repeated time check; A5 accepts B escort with another assigned access task and offers to hold bags.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 time and ticket settle departure timing; B4 escort makes asking about B own access a coherent new detail, without asserting any actual ticket rule.

relationship.evidence: B2 objects to repetition and B4 offers practical accompaniment while naming the personal fear.

heightening.evidence: B4 solution becomes A5 concern about the companion ticket, keeping attention away from leaving B.

specificity.evidence: A1 move, B2 train time and B4 leaving me make both logistics and separation stakes clear.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 permission, new check and bag-holding offer enact the negotiation; no line explains the card combination.

reservation: A does not admit the underlying fear. The repeated practical management makes avoidance visible without requiring the assessment to diagnose a particular fear.
